title: Sepsis in people aged 16 and over
blurb: Use NICE NG253 to grade sepsis risk from NEWS2, deliver the high-risk bundle within the hour, give 250 mL fluid boluses and know the medium and low risk pathways.
question: Ms Begum, 54, has a urinary infection on a medical ward. At 10:00 her NEWS2 is 8. By when must IV antibiotics be given, and what fluid bolus does NICE NG253 describe?

teach.body: Sepsis is a life-threatening reaction to an infection that damages the body's own organs. NICE NG253 (2025, replacing NG51) covers people aged 16 or over who are not pregnant or recently pregnant; separate NICE guidance covers under 16s and pregnancy. It asks you to think 'could this be sepsis?' whenever someone with possible infection is unwell, to use NEWS2 to grade risk in acute hospitals, acute mental health settings and ambulances, and to listen to concerns from the person and their family.

teach.h: Factors that raise risk or delay recognition (rec 1.2.1)
head: Group
Examples
rows: Frailty, multimorbidity, impaired immunity, surgery or invasive procedure in past 6 weeks
Indwelling catheters, breach of skin integrity, repeated antibiotics
Learning disability, cognitive impairment, needing an interpreter
teach.caption: In people with learning disability or dementia, a change in behaviour may be the sign. Pulse oximeters can overestimate SpO2 in darker skin.
A single parameter scoring 3: request a high-priority review by a clinician at FY2 level or above for a definite decision on risk.

teach.h: When the score underestimates the danger
teach.body: Consider the person at higher risk than their NEWS2 suggests if they look mottled or ashen, have a non-blanching petechial or purpuric rash, or cyanosis of skin, lips or tongue, or if they have deteriorated or not improved since a previous score or intervention. Do not rely on fever or hypothermia to rule sepsis in or out, and remember beta-blockers can blunt a rising heart rate.

head: Risk
Recalculate
teach.caption: Also recalculate whenever the person deteriorates or changes unexpectedly (rec 1.6.6).

steps.label: Urgent review
steps.sub: Clinician FY2 or above; think of other diagnoses

steps.label: Venous bloods
steps.sub: Gas with glucose and lactate, culture, FBC, CRP, U&E, creatinine, LFTs, clotting

steps.label: IV antibiotics
steps.sub: Broad-spectrum, within 1 hour of calculating NEWS2

steps.label: IV fluid bolus
steps.sub: Without delay, within 1 hour, unless contraindicated

steps.label: No response in 1 hour?
steps.sub: Senior attends in person; critical care; inform consultant

teach.caption: Oxygen: target 94–98%, or 88–92% if at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure (rec 1.10.1).

items.label: initial bolus of isotonic crystalloid (Hartmann's, or 0.9% saline)
ideal time to give each bolus
total, including earlier fluids, before senior advice
reassess the person after each one

rows.label: Review
values: FY2+ reviews person and lactate within 1 h

rows.label: Antibiotics
values: FY2+ may defer up to 3 h
FY2+ may defer up to 6 h

rows.label: Changes plan
values: Lactate over 2 or AKI: treat as high risk

teach.caption: Deferral windows are timed from the first NEWS2 score on initial assessment or ward deterioration, and are used to gather information for a more specific diagnosis.

teach.h: Worked example: Ms Begum on a medical ward
items: 10:00: suspected urinary infection, NEWS2 8: high risk. The nurse escalates immediately for an FY2+ review and starts 30-minute NEWS2 recalculation.
10:10: venous gas (lactate 3.4 mmol/L, glucose 7.1), blood culture and the other bloods are taken; oxygen started to 94–98%.
10:25: 250 mL Hartmann's over 10–15 minutes; she is reassessed and a second 250 mL bolus is given as prescribed.
10:40: IV broad-spectrum antibiotic given, within 1 hour of the 10:00 NEWS2. If she has not responded by about 11:00, a senior must attend in person and critical care is involved.

teach.text: NG51 is withdrawn. Under NG253 risk is graded by NEWS2, the initial bolus is 250 mL (not 500 mL), and the antibiotic clock starts when the NEWS2 score is calculated, not when the person arrived or when bloods were taken.

items: NG253: 16 and over, not pregnant or recently pregnant; NEWS2 7+ high, 5–6 medium, 1–4 low, 0 very low.
Single parameter of 3: high-priority FY2+ review; mottled, rash or cyanosis: think higher risk.
High risk: bloods including lactate and culture, IV antibiotics and fluids within 1 hour, NEWS2 every 30 minutes.
Fluids: 250 mL crystalloid over 10–15 min, reassess, up to 1,000 mL, then senior advice.
Medium: antibiotics may be deferred up to 3 h (not if lactate over 2 or AKI); low: up to 6 h.

summary: You can now recognise people at risk of sepsis, grade their risk with NEWS2 under NICE NG253, and deliver the high-risk bundle of bloods, antibiotics and 250 mL fluid boluses within the hour. You know the medium and low risk pathways, when deferral is allowed, and when to escalate to senior and critical care help.

A.q: Mr Ford, 70, has suspected sepsis and a NEWS2 of 8. How often should his NEWS2 be recalculated under NICE NG253?
options: Every 30 minutes
Every hour
Every 4–6 hours
Every 15 minutes
A.why: NG253 rec 1.6.5: recalculate every 30 minutes for those at high risk (NEWS2 7 or more).

whyNot.1: Hourly recalculation is for medium risk (NEWS2 5–6).
whyNot.2: Every 4–6 hours is for low risk (NEWS2 1–4).
whyNot.3: NG253 sets 30 minutes for high risk; 15 minutes is not the specified interval.

A.q: Which person has a factor that NICE NG253 says increases the risk of sepsis or of it being missed?
options: Mrs Lee, 70, who had a flu vaccine yesterday
Mr Day, 68, who had surgery 4 months ago
Mr Ade, 50, who had bowel surgery 3 weeks ago
Ms Rao, 40, who runs three times a week
A.why: NG253 rec 1.2.1 lists surgery or invasive procedures in the past 6 weeks among the factors that increase risk.

whyNot.0: A vaccine is not one of the listed risk factors, and 70 is below the age factor of 75 or over.
whyNot.1: Surgery 4 months ago is outside the 6-week window.
whyNot.3: Regular exercise is not a risk factor for sepsis.

A.q: A doctor prescribes fluid resuscitation for a woman of 30, not pregnant, with suspected sepsis. Which type of fluid does NICE NG253 recommend?
options: An albumin solution such as 4.5% HAS
A balanced crystalloid, e.g. Hartmann's
A glucose solution such as 5% glucose
A colloid such as a gelatin solution
A.why: NG253 rec 1.8.5: use an isotonic electrolyte crystalloid, a balanced solution such as Hartmann's, or 0.9% saline if a balanced solution is not available.

whyNot.0: Albumin is not the NG253 first-line resuscitation fluid.
whyNot.2: 5% glucose is not an isotonic electrolyte crystalloid for resuscitation.
whyNot.3: Colloids are not the fluid NG253 recommends.

B.q: Mr Kaur, 63, has suspected chest infection and a NEWS2 of 5. His venous lactate is 1.4 mmol/L and he has no acute kidney injury. What does NICE NG253 allow regarding antibiotics?
options: They must be given within 1 hour
An FY2+ may defer them for up to 6 hours
They wait until blood cultures are back
An FY2+ may defer them for up to 3 hours
B.why: NG253 rec 1.8.17: for medium risk without hypoperfusion, a clinician at FY2 or above may consider deferring antibiotics for up to 3 hours after the first NEWS2 score to gather information; once decided, do not delay.

whyNot.0: The 1-hour rule applies to high risk, or to medium risk with hypoperfusion.
whyNot.1: Up to 6 hours is the deferral window for low risk.
whyNot.2: Waiting for culture results would delay treatment far beyond NG253's windows.

B.q: Mrs Hart, 72, has suspected sepsis with a NEWS2 of 4. Two hours later, after fluids and assessment, her NEWS2 is still 4 and she looks no better. How should her risk be viewed under NICE NG253?
options: As higher than her score suggests
As unchanged low risk, as the score is stable
As very low, as she has had treatment
As resolved, so observations can be reduced
B.why: NG253 rec 1.6.4: consider the risk higher than NEWS2 alone suggests if there has been deterioration or no improvement since a previous score or intervention.

whyNot.1: A stable score after intervention is a lack of improvement, which NG253 says should raise concern.
whyNot.2: Having had treatment does not lower her risk when she has not improved.
whyNot.3: No improvement is not resolution; reducing observations would be unsafe.

B.q: Mr Patel, 45, has suspected infection with a NEWS2 of 2. Under NICE NG253, who should review him and within what time?
options: A registered health practitioner within 1 hour
The critical care team within 1 hour
A consultant physician within 30 minutes
His GP at the next routine appointment
B.why: NG253 rec 1.8.22: for low risk, arrange review by a registered health practitioner within 1 hour of being assessed as low risk.

whyNot.1: Critical care input is for high-risk people, not a NEWS2 of 2.
whyNot.2: Consultant involvement is for high-risk people not responding to treatment.
whyNot.3: A routine GP appointment is far too slow for suspected sepsis in hospital.

C.q: Mrs Ahmed, 66, is high risk with suspected sepsis. An hour after antibiotics and fluid boluses she remains hypotensive and drowsy. What does NICE NG253 require now?
options: A senior attends in person; critical care involved
A further 1,000 mL bolus and recheck in 1 hour
Recalculate NEWS2 in 4 hours to see the trend
Change to a broader antibiotic and observe
C.why: NG253 rec 1.8.15: if a high-risk person does not respond within 1 hour of any intervention, ensure the senior clinical decision maker attends in person, refer to or discuss with critical care, and inform the consultant.

whyNot.1: Boluses are 250 mL, with senior advice after 1,000 mL; a litre bolus is not NG253 practice.
whyNot.2: High-risk people need NEWS2 every 30 minutes, not 4-hourly.
whyNot.3: Changing antibiotics does not replace the senior and critical care escalation NG253 requires.

C.q: Mr Stone, 59, has suspected sepsis. He has received four 250 mL boluses of Hartmann's, reassessed after each, and his blood pressure has not improved enough. What is the next step under NICE NG253?
options: Give a further 500 mL bolus over 15 minutes
Give 250 mL boluses until his BP is normal
Get advice from a senior clinical decision maker
Stop fluids and continue hourly observations
C.why: NG253 rec 1.8.9: if the person has not improved enough after 1,000 mL has been given, get advice from a senior clinical decision maker.

whyNot.0: 500 mL boluses belong to general resuscitation advice; NG253 uses 250 mL and caps at 1,000 mL before senior advice.
whyNot.1: NG253 sets a 1,000 mL total before senior advice, not open-ended boluses.
whyNot.3: Stopping without senior input leaves a non-responding person without a plan.

C.q: Mr Jones, 52, has a chest infection. His NEWS2 is 3, all from a respiration rate of 27. The FY2 judges the high rate is due to the infection. How should he be managed under NICE NG253?
options: As low risk, as his total is 3
As very low risk with routine observations
As low risk, deferring antibiotics up to 6 hours
As medium or high risk, as infection is the cause
C.why: NG253 rec 1.8.24: with a NEWS2 of 3 or 4 and a single parameter scoring 3, if the likely cause is the infection, manage as medium or high risk and give antibiotics in line with those recommendations.

whyNot.0: Low-risk management applies only if the 3 points are due to something else, such as a pre-existing condition.
whyNot.1: A total of 3 is not very low risk (which is a score of 0).
whyNot.2: Six-hour deferral is the low-risk pathway, which does not apply when the infection causes the 3 points.

reteach.title: One number, four doors
reteach.question: Think of NEWS2 as the key that opens one of four doors. What is behind each door?

blocks.body: Score 7 or more: the high-risk door: FY2+ now, bloods with lactate and culture, antibiotics and 250 mL fluid within the hour, NEWS2 every 30 minutes. Score 5–6: medium: review within the hour, antibiotics may wait up to 3 hours unless lactate is over 2 or the kidneys are injured. Score 1–4: low: review within the hour, antibiotics may wait up to 6 hours. Score 0: very low. A mottled look, a rash or no improvement pushes you up a door.

items.label: IV antibiotics and fluid bolus given

blocks.text: Hypoperfusion turns medium into high: a lactate over 2 mmol/L or acute kidney injury means treat as high risk.

explain.body: NEWS2 7+ high, 5–6 medium, 1–4 low, 0 very low. A single parameter scoring 3 needs a high-priority FY2+ review.

test.q: Under NICE NG253, what risk does a NEWS2 of 6 suggest in a person with suspected infection?
options: Low risk
Medium risk
High risk
Very low risk
test.why: NG253 rec 1.6.2: a score of 5 or 6 suggests medium risk of severe illness or death from sepsis.

whyNot.0: Low risk is a score of 1–4.
whyNot.2: High risk is a score of 7 or more.
whyNot.3: Very low risk is a score of 0.

explain.body: Mottled or ashen skin, a non-blanching rash, cyanosis, or no improvement or deterioration since a previous score or intervention: consider higher risk.

test.q: Which finding should make the nurse consider a person's sepsis risk higher than their NEWS2 suggests?
options: A temperature of 37.9 °C
Cyanosis of the lips
A pulse of 88 per minute
Mild nausea after eating
test.why: NG253 rec 1.6.3: cyanosis of skin, lips or tongue, mottled or ashen appearance, or a non-blanching rash suggest higher risk than NEWS2 alone.

whyNot.0: This temperature scores 0 on NEWS2 and is not one of the higher-risk signs.
whyNot.2: A pulse of 88 scores 0 and is not a higher-risk sign.
whyNot.3: Mild nausea is not one of the NG253 higher-risk signs.

explain.body: For high risk, give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour of calculating the NEWS2 score that identified the risk.

test.q: For a high-risk person with suspected sepsis, the 1-hour antibiotic target is timed from when?
options: Arrival at the hospital
When blood cultures are taken
Calculation of the NEWS2 score
The doctor's first review
test.why: NG253: give broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour of calculating the NEWS2 score.

whyNot.0: Arrival time is not the NG253 starting point; a person may deteriorate later on a ward.
whyNot.1: Cultures are taken within the hour but do not start the clock.
whyNot.3: Waiting for a review to start the clock could delay antibiotics.

explain.body: Isotonic crystalloid, 250 mL boluses ideally over 10–15 minutes, reassessing after each, up to 1,000 mL in total including earlier fluids, then senior advice if not improved.

test.q: Under NICE NG253, after what total volume of bolus fluid should senior advice be sought if the person has not improved enough?
options: 500 mL
750 mL
test.why: NG253 recs 1.8.7 and 1.8.9: give further 250 mL boluses up to 1,000 mL in total, and seek senior advice if not improved after 1,000 mL.

whyNot.0: 500 mL is the general RCUK bolus size, not the NG253 limit before senior advice.
whyNot.2: 2,000 mL exceeds the NG253 total before senior advice.
whyNot.3: 750 mL is three boluses; NG253 allows up to four before seeking advice.
